_readme: Conteúdo curado da demo pública — a fonte de verdade do que o visitante vê.
REGRA EDITORIAL, e não é decorativa: nada aqui pode ser sobre metadados.
Contagens de linhas, tabelas mais usadas e resumos de esquema estão
proibidos. Foi exactamente esse tipo de resposta — 'resumo de alto nível:
contagem de linhas e tabelas mais usadas' — que arruinou a primeira
impressão da demo antiga. Cada título aqui responde a uma pergunta que um
COO faria em voz alta, e cada número tem SQL por trás que o produz.
O `executed_sql` não é decoração: é verificado contra a base sintética
antes de persistir (--verify-sql). Conteúdo que afirme um número que o
seu próprio SQL não devolve é pior do que não ter conteúdo nenhum — numa
demo comercial, um número errado que o prospect consegue conferir custa

datasets.name: Northwind Cloud — SaaS B2B
datasets.description: CRM, marketing, finance, web analytics and product usage for a fictional B2B SaaS. 5 connected schemas.

insight.title: Enterprise accounts paying for seats they stopped using
insight.summary: Enterprise accounts are billing more seats than they log into. Seat utilisation is the earliest churn signal there is — it moves months before the cancellation email, and it is visible today across CRM, billing and product usage at once.

stat_tiles.label: Enterprise accounts under 60% seat use
stat_tiles.value_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM crm.accounts a JOIN finance.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.id AND s.cancelled_at IS NULL JOIN product_usage.account_health h ON h.account_id = a.id WHERE a.plan = 'enterprise' AND h.seats_paid > 0 AND h.seats_used < 0.6 * h.seats_paid

stat_tiles.label: Monthly revenue exposed
stat_tiles.value_sql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(s.monthly_amount), 0) FROM crm.accounts a JOIN finance.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.id AND s.cancelled_at IS NULL JOIN product_usage.account_health h ON h.account_id = a.id WHERE a.plan = 'enterprise' AND h.seats_paid > 0 AND h.seats_used < 0.6 * h.seats_paid

stat_tiles.label: Avg. seat utilisation
stat_tiles.value_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(100.0 * h.seats_used / NULLIF(h.seats_paid, 0)), 1) FROM crm.accounts a JOIN product_usage.account_health h ON h.account_id = a.id WHERE a.plan = 'enterprise' AND h.seats_paid > 0

sources.description: Seats paid vs seats actually used

insight.executed_sql:
SELECT a.name,
       s.monthly_amount,
       h.seats_paid,
       h.seats_used,
       ROUND(100.0 * h.seats_used / NULLIF(h.seats_paid, 0), 1) AS seat_utilisation_pct
FROM crm.accounts a
JOIN finance.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.id AND s.cancelled_at IS NULL
JOIN product_usage.account_health h ON h.account_id = a.id
WHERE a.plan = 'enterprise'
  AND h.seats_paid > 0
  AND h.seats_used < 0.6 * h.seats_paid
ORDER BY s.monthly_amount DESC
insight.series_sql:
SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', i.issued_at)::date AS t,
       SUM(i.amount)                             AS v
FROM finance.invoices i
WHERE i.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

qas.question: Which customers are most likely to churn, and what revenue is at stake?
qas.answer_markdown:
Accounts flagged **risk** or **churn** by health score, ranked by the monthly revenue they still pay.

What makes this actionable rather than interesting: it joins the health signal to the money. A low health score on a small account is noise; the same score on the largest subscription in the book is a board-level problem.

The accounts at the top of this list are still paying. That is the window.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT a.name,
       a.plan,
       h.risk_level,
       h.score,
       s.monthly_amount,
       h.last_login_at
FROM product_usage.account_health h
JOIN crm.accounts a         ON a.id = h.account_id
JOIN finance.subscriptions s ON s.account_id = a.id AND s.cancelled_at IS NULL
WHERE h.risk_level IN ('risk', 'churn')
ORDER BY s.monthly_amount DESC
LIMIT 10

qas.question: Which marketing channel actually produces revenue, not just leads?
qas.answer_markdown:
Spend per channel against **closed-won** revenue traced back through the lead that opened the deal.

The distinction matters. Channels that produce many leads and few deals look excellent on a marketing dashboard and lose money in the ledger — the cost per lead is flattering, the cost per euro of revenue is not.

This follows the chain end to end: campaign spend → lead → opportunity → closed-won amount.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT c.channel,
       SUM(DISTINCT c.spend)                                    AS spend,
       COUNT(DISTINCT l.id)                                     AS leads,
       COUNT(DISTINCT o.id) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won') AS deals_won,
       COALESCE(SUM(o.amount) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won'), 0) AS revenue_won
FROM marketing.campaigns c
LEFT JOIN marketing.leads l   ON l.campaign_id = c.id
LEFT JOIN crm.opportunities o ON o.id = l.converted_to_opportunity_id
GROUP BY c.channel
ORDER BY revenue_won DESC

qas.question: How much revenue is sitting in overdue invoices, and who owes it?
qas.answer_markdown:
Overdue invoices by account, oldest first.

Cash that has been earned and not collected is the cheapest cash in the business — no discount, no new deal, no campaign. It only needs someone to know it exists.

The join to the account name is the whole point: an invoice ID is not something anyone can act on, a customer name with a phone number is.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT a.name,
       i.issued_at,
       i.amount,
       CURRENT_DATE - i.issued_at AS days_outstanding
FROM finance.invoices i
JOIN finance.subscriptions s ON s.id = i.subscription_id
JOIN crm.accounts a          ON a.id = s.account_id
WHERE i.status = 'overdue'
ORDER BY i.issued_at ASC
LIMIT 15

qas.question: What is the win rate, and how long does a deal take to close?
qas.answer_markdown:
Win rate and average cycle length per plan tier.

The two numbers belong together. A high win rate with a long cycle and a lower win rate with a short one are very different businesses, and reporting either alone hides which one you are.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT a.plan,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won')  AS won,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_lost') AS lost,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won')
             / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.stage IN ('closed_won','closed_lost')), 0), 1) AS win_rate_pct,
       ROUND(AVG(o.amount) FILTER (WHERE o.stage = 'closed_won'), 2) AS avg_won_amount
FROM crm.opportunities o
JOIN crm.accounts a ON a.id = o.account_id
GROUP BY a.plan
ORDER BY win_rate_pct DESC NULLS LAST

qas.question: Which product features do our healthiest customers use that the at-risk ones don't?
qas.answer_markdown:
Feature adoption split by health band.

The gap between the two columns is the onboarding backlog. A feature that healthy accounts use heavily and at-risk accounts never touched is not a product problem — it is a feature nobody showed them.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT f.feature_name,
       ROUND(AVG(f.times_used_30d) FILTER (WHERE h.risk_level = 'healthy'), 1)          AS healthy_avg_uses,
       ROUND(AVG(f.times_used_30d) FILTER (WHERE h.risk_level IN ('risk','churn')), 1)  AS at_risk_avg_uses,
       COUNT(DISTINCT f.account_id)                                                     AS accounts_using
FROM product_usage.feature_adoption f
JOIN product_usage.account_health h ON h.account_id = f.account_id
GROUP BY f.feature_name
ORDER BY healthy_avg_uses DESC NULLS LAST

qas.question: Where does our website traffic come from, and does it convert?
qas.answer_markdown:
Sessions by acquisition source against the accounts that ended up signing.

Traffic without the conversion column is a vanity number. The two together tell you which source to buy more of.
qas.executed_sql:
SELECT COALESCE(s.utm_source, 'direct')                     AS source,
       COUNT(*)                                            AS sessions,
       COUNT(DISTINCT s.account_id)                        AS known_accounts,
       ROUND(AVG(s.pages_viewed), 1)                       AS avg_pages
FROM web_analytics.sessions s
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY sessions DESC
